title: Cet enfant est le mien  (That Child is Mine)

segments.t: At a Cannes hotel bar, agency boss Hicham confronts Andrea after discovering that she is pregnant following their intimate night together. Claiming biological fatherhood, Hicham insists on having a say in the pregnancy, while Andrea fiercely defends her exclusive bodily autonomy. Listen to the scene in French first.
Salut, Andréa! Tu viens d'arriver?
Oui, je viens d'arriver au bar.
Rien ne vaut ces belles fraises.
Je prendrai une coupe de champagne.
Tu allais me le dire quand?
Je parle de ton bébé.
Inutile de mentir, je sais tout!
Ça ne te regarde pas du tout.
Ça me regarde tout à fait!
Je suis le père de cet enfant.
Quel enfant? Il n'y a personne!
Il y a juste moi et mon corps.
C'est moi qui décide, d'accord?
Tu ne décides pas toute seule.
Cet enfant est aussi le mien!
Let's walk through the conversation step by step.
Salut, Andréa! Tu viens d'arriver?
'Hi, Andrea! Did you just arrive?' Literally 'you come of to-arrive,' French uses 'come from' plus an action to describe something that just happened seconds ago!
Oui, je viens d'arriver au bar.
'Yes, I just arrived at the bar.' Andrea mirrors that exact 'come from arriving' expression in French, followed by contracted 'at the bar.'
Rien ne vaut ces belles fraises.
'Nothing beats these lovely strawberries.' Literally 'nothing is worth these lovely strawberries,' a classic French compliment for top-notch food or drink.
Je prendrai une coupe de champagne.
'I will have a glass of champagne.' For bubbly, French specifies a wide 'goblet/coupe' rather than an ordinary tumbler, introduced by polite future 'I will take.'
Tu allais me le dire quand?
'When were you going to tell me?' Notice casual French tucking the question word 'when' right at the end instead of leading with it as in English.
Je parle de ton bébé.
'I am talking about your baby.' Where English says 'talk about,' French links 'speak' with 'of'—literally 'I speak of your baby.'
Inutile de mentir, je sais tout!
'No use lying, I know everything!' Opening with 'useless of to-lie' skips 'it is' in French for a sharp, urgent confrontation.
Ça ne te regarde pas du tout.
'That is none of your business at all.' Literally 'that does not look-at you at all,' this unforgettable idiom is how you'll hear French speakers say 'mind your own business!'
Ça me regarde tout à fait!
'It concerns me completely!' Hicham flips her exact 'look-at' idiom into the positive and caps it with a three-word chunk that means 'completely' or 'quite so.'
Je suis le père de cet enfant.
'I am the father of that child.' Before vowel-initial 'child,' masculine 'this/that' adds a 't' in French so the two words link smoothly aloud.
Quel enfant? Il n'y a personne!
'What child? There is nobody!' In the negative, 'there has nobody' drops the usual 'not' partner 'step' because 'nobody' completes the negation on its own.
Il y a juste moi et mon corps.
'There is just me and my body.' Using 'there has' again in French, Andrea pairs emphatic 'me' with 'my body' for blunt clarity.
C'est moi qui décide, d'accord?
'I am the one who decides, okay?' Framing 'me' inside 'it is... who' is how speakers spotlight 'I'm the one who' in French rather than stressing plain 'I' by voice.
Tu ne décides pas toute seule.
'You do not decide all alone.' Because Hicham addresses Andrea, both 'all' and 'alone' pick up feminine endings that you can actually hear pronounced in French!
Cet enfant est aussi le mien!

'That child is mine as well!' Standalone 'mine' in French ALWAYS keeps 'the' in front—literally 'the mine'—matching 'child' in gender. Now let's listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.
Salut, Andréa! Tu viens d'arriver?
Oui, je viens d'arriver au bar.
Rien ne vaut ces belles fraises.
Je prendrai une coupe de champagne.
Tu allais me le dire quand?
Je parle de ton bébé.
Inutile de mentir, je sais tout!
Ça ne te regarde pas du tout.
Ça me regarde tout à fait!
Je suis le père de cet enfant.
Quel enfant? Il n'y a personne!
Il y a juste moi et mon corps.
C'est moi qui décide, d'accord?
Tu ne décides pas toute seule.
Cet enfant est aussi le mien!
Fiercely asserting her bodily autonomy, Andrea rejects Hicham's demands to participate in decisions about her pregnancy. See you next time!
Bonne soirée!
